svg.title: Preliminary observation requirements; no world surface footprints
svg.text: A: orange wall / pale bank / green contact · north up · confirmed D: 0

a.title: Station 0 / window 0000: A bank; B present; C absent. Close left bank and tunnel-side ground contrast with a broad mountain face and skyline. No distinct farther terrain region is established beyond the dominant face itself.

Station 1 / window 0000: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Steeper left roadside face and reverse banks sit below a prominent mountain outline. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 2 / window 0000: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Tall left face is close; reverse shows banks, a projecting peak and the tunnel approach. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 3 / window 0001: A wall; B present; C present. High left cut and lower opposite bank frame large rock faces; reverse opens toward a distinct peak. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 4 / window 0001: A wall; B present; C present. Left wall rises immediately beside the road; reverse shows an open peak beyond lower banks. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 5 / window 0002: A wall; B present; C present. Very tall face dominates the bend; reverse includes the same kind of close contact plus an open ridge. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 6 / window 0002: A wall; B present; C absent. Tall roadside faces and upper rock planes fill the paired views without a clear distant skyline. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 7 / window 0003: A wall; B present; C absent. Close left and reverse-right walls constrain the road; broad upper faces fill the background. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 8 / window 0003: A wall; B present; C absent. High side wall and smaller opposing bank remain close; a small ridge is visible in reverse. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 9 / window 0003: A wall; B present; C absent. Reverse-right wall dominates while the forward bend exposes lower banks and upper rock masses. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 10 / window 0003: A wall; B present; C present. Large sloped-to-steep roadside face, a lower outer bank and coastal opening are readable. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 11 / window 0003: A wall; B present; C present. Close side faces persist while the forward view opens across the valley toward the coast. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.
Station 12 / window 0004: A wall; B present; C present. Tall left face with broad upper rock planes; reverse retains a right face and wider valley context.
Station 13 / window 0004: A wall; B present; C present. Substantial uphill wall continues at contact distance with a coastal gap and reverse rock bands.
Station 14 / window 0004: A wall; B present; C present. Large nearby cliff planes dominate above the road; reverse reveals layered valley faces.

Station 15 / window 0004: A wall; B present; C uncertain. The bend brings a broad high face close; reverse keeps the side wall and more distant rock bands. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 16 / window 0005: A wall; B present; C absent. Reverse broad wall fills the bend; forward looks into a rock enclosure with limited skyline evidence. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 17 / window 0005: A bank; B present; C uncertain. Lower sloped contact regions flank the road while an upper cliff face remains prominent in reverse. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence. Raised-side extent on the bend is unresolved.
Station 18 / window 0005: A wall; B present; C present. Forward-right face becomes steep and close; reverse-left contact sits below a broad rock face.
Station 19 / window 0005: A wall; B present; C present. Close faceted right wall contrasts with reverse upper cliff planes and a small coastal opening.
Station 20 / window 0006: A bank; B absent; C present. Lower roadside slopes lead into an open mountain panorama; no separate face dominates the pair.
Station 21 / window 0006: A wall; B absent; C present. Short close cut walls are readable while the distant peak remains a skyline element.

Station 22 / window 0007: A bank; B absent; C present. Low sloping banks wrap the bend; reverse opens toward a modest distant peak. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 23 / window 0007: A bank; B absent; C present. Banks and road contact dominate nearby, with a small peak and open sky beyond. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 24 / window 0008: A bank; B absent; C absent. Low banks wrap the turn; reverse shows an open ridge above a long shallow roadside cut. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 25 / window 0008: A wall; B absent; C present. Forward-left cut is steep at contact distance, but the principal distant feature is the coastal outlook. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 26 / window 0009: A wall; B present; C absent. Reverse has a broad close wall; forward faces a large rocky enclosure with limited skyline. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence. Raised-side extent on the bend is unresolved.
Station 27 / window 0009: A wall; B present; C present. Left roadside cut and reverse-right upper cliff accompany a broad forward rock face and sea opening.
Station 28 / window 0009: A wall; B present; C present. Long near cut walls and a large forward enclosing face contrast with the reverse coast.
Station 29 / window 0009: A wall; B present; C present. Close left wall continues; a substantial upper face remains forward and the coast opens behind.
Station 30 / window 0009: A wall; B present; C present. Forward cliff enclosure remains prominent above a close cut; reverse is more open toward the coast.

Station 31 / window 0010: A bank; B absent; C present. Low sloped contact banks and a broad coastal opening; no isolated dominant wall is clear. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.
Station 32 / window 0010: A bank; B absent; C present. Near slope switches sides with direction; reverse has an open horizon and smaller ridge context.

Station 33 / window 0011: A bank; B absent; C uncertain. The bend is bordered by low banks; broad slope divisions matter more than a dominant wall. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 34 / window 0011: A bank; B absent; C absent. Near banks remain low; a small ridge and broad slope occupy the background. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 35 / window 0011: A wall; B absent; C uncertain. A steeper roadside segment emerges, but background face dominance and skyline are unclear at contact-sheet scale. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 36 / window 0012: A wall; B present; C present. Reverse close high wall has readable large planes; forward opens toward the coast and outer ridge. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 37 / window 0012: A bank; B uncertain; C present. Lower banks frame the road; the reverse upper face may need broader-form attention, requiring original review. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 38 / window 0012: A bank; B absent; C present. Low banks and broad sloped rock forms accompany the coastal outlook without a dominating face. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 39 / window 0012: A bank; B absent; C present. Slanted near banks and broad hillside divisions are visible; forward includes the open coast. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.
Station 40 / window 0012: A bank; B absent; C present. Readable near left and reverse-right banks sit below broad slopes and an open coastal horizon.
Station 41 / window 0012: A bank; B absent; C present. Near contact is a sloping bank; distant coast and low outcrops supply the wider composition.
Station 42 / window 0012: A bank; B absent; C present. Shallow-to-moderate side banks remain close, with an open coast and small forward outcrop.
Station 43 / window 0013: A bank; B absent; C present. Same transition to lower banks persists; far outlines remain distinct from close contact detail.

Station 44 / window 0013: A bank; B absent; C present. Both forward banks are readable at the bend; reverse right bank leads into a broad hillside. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 45 / window 0013: A bank; B absent; C present. Low near banks accompany an open coastal view; distant rocky forms are not dominant walls. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 46 / window 0013: A bank; B absent; C present. Open coastal bend with low banks; reverse slope has broad material-scale structure rather than a dominant face. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 47 / window 0013: A bank; B present; C absent. A broad rocky face becomes prominent in reverse beyond the low roadside banks. No distinct farther terrain region is established beyond the dominant face itself. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 48 / window 0013: A wall; B present; C absent. Near left cut steepens; a broad rocky face and skyline dominate the reverse outlook. No distinct farther terrain region is established beyond the dominant face itself. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.
Station 49 / window 0014: A wall; B absent; C present. Close cut switches sides with direction; open coast and a modest outcrop form the distant context.
Station 50 / window 0014: A wall; B absent; C present. Strong close wall and its base contact are visible; the outer peak reads mainly as an outline.
Station 51 / window 0014: A wall; B absent; C present. Tall local wall persists but the wider view is chiefly coast, ridge and sloping ground.
Station 52 / window 0015: A wall; B absent; C present. Steep roadside face is close; reverse includes broad hillside divisions without an isolated dominant face.
Station 53 / window 0015: A wall; B absent; C present. Near wall remains readable; open coast and layered hillside carry the farther composition.
Station 54 / window 0015: A bank; B absent; C present. Roadside forms become more sloped; coast and broad valley bands remain visible.
Station 55 / window 0015: A bank; B absent; C present. Sloping contact bank leads toward coast; reverse shows broad terrain bands rather than a dominant wall.
Station 56 / window 0016: A wall; B present; C present. A large tall roadside wall fills much of both views while the coastal horizon remains visible.
Station 57 / window 0016: A wall; B present; C present. Broad close wall and its upper contour stay dominant on the outside of the turn.

Station 58 / window 0017: A wall; B present; C present. Reverse large wall spans the turn; forward provides an open skyline and lower contact banks. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence. Raised-side extent on the bend is unresolved.

Station 59 / window 0017: A bank; B present; C present. Near banks are lower, but a large reverse rocky mass with readable broad planes is prominent. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.
Station 60 / window 0017: A bank; B present; C present. Sloping near contacts sit below a substantial reverse mountain face and open coast forward.
Station 61 / window 0017: A bank; B present; C present. Near banks continue while a broad reverse rocky face and coast retain separate visual roles.
Station 62 / window 0017: A wall; B present; C present. Local cut steepens on the left; the reverse upper rocky face remains compositionally prominent.
Station 63 / window 0018: A wall; B present; C present. Steep local side cut plus a dominant reverse mountain face; coast is visible forward.
Station 64 / window 0018: A wall; B present; C present. Close cut planes remain readable; reverse mountain face and forward coast warrant broad-form review.
Station 65 / window 0019: A wall; B present; C present. Tall near side cut and a distant-but-prominent reverse face coexist with the coastal panorama.
Station 66 / window 0019: A wall; B present; C present. Close wall persists and broad reverse rocky planes remain dominant above the route.

Station 67 / window 0020: A wall; B present; C present. Long upper face dominates the forward enclosure; reverse opens to sea beside a close side wall. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 68 / window 0020: A wall; B present; C present. Same wall-to-open-coast contrast remains, with readable base contact in both directions. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 69 / window 0021: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Close wall at the bend and a large reverse rocky mass combine local and broad-form needs. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 70 / window 0021: A bank; B present; C absent. Lower contact banks at the turn reveal a dominant mountain face forward and high faces in reverse. No distinct farther terrain region is established beyond the dominant face itself. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 71 / window 0021: A bank; B present; C uncertain. Slanted near contacts switch sides; a large mountain face remains prominent in forward view. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 72 / window 0021: A bank; B present; C uncertain. Low-to-moderate banks flank the bend beneath a dominant rocky face; reverse opens to coast. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 73 / window 0021: A bank; B present; C absent. Sloping contact banks and a substantial forward mountain mass coexist with the coastal opening. No distinct farther terrain region is established beyond the dominant face itself. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 74 / window 0021: A bank; B present; C absent. Original forward PNG shows a large outer rocky face with readable broad planes and a strong outline. This is a dominant-face requirement; the face's own skyline and sea do not establish a separate C terrain region. Low local banks remain distinct. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 75 / window 0022: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Low banks frame the same outer peak and coast; evaluate peak dominance on the original image. The outer peak needs B-versus-C confirmation; its own outline does not establish both. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 76 / window 0022: A bank; B present; C uncertain. Near banks are low while the reverse rocky face occupies a substantial part of the composition. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 77 / window 0022: A bank; B present; C uncertain. Sloped contact and open coast contrast with the broad, readable reverse mountain face. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 78 / window 0023: A bank; B present; C uncertain. Low local banks lead toward a large reverse cliff mass and a coastal horizon. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 79 / window 0023: A bank; B present; C absent. Contact banks remain modest but a large reverse rocky face has readable major divisions. No distinct farther terrain region is established beyond the dominant face itself. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 80 / window 0023: A bank; B present; C uncertain. Near slopes stay low-to-moderate; reverse mountain face and skyline remain prominent. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.
Station 81 / window 0023: A wall; B present; C present. A close cut steepens while large upper faces and the reverse mountain outline remain readable.
Station 82 / window 0023: A wall; B present; C present. Tall near side cut leads below a large high face; reverse opens around the peak silhouette.

Station 83 / window 0024: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Large near wall and upper cliff planes are clear, with a distinct reverse skyline. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 84 / window 0024: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Tall nearby face and reverse upper mass both carry readable large forms and outline. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 85 / window 0025: A wall; B present; C uncertain. High near wall fills much of the view; reverse adds a large rocky peak silhouette. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 86 / window 0025: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Close wall remains dominant with an open view of the reverse ridge above it. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 87 / window 0025: A wall; B present; C absent. Near tall wall and its major planes remain important beside the distant peak outline. No distinct farther terrain region is established beyond the dominant face itself.

Station 88 / window 0026: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Close wall persists and a broad reverse cliff mass is readable beyond the road. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 89 / window 0026: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Near side face has large readable planes; reverse mountain mass and skyline remain prominent. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 90 / window 0026: A wall; B present; C absent. Tall local face continues with layered mountain faces and a distinct reverse peak beyond. No distinct farther terrain region is established beyond the dominant face itself.

Station 91 / window 0027: A wall; B present; C absent. Close steep side cut wraps the bend; reverse upper wall and rocky skyline are prominent. No distinct farther terrain region is established beyond the dominant face itself.

Station 92 / window 0027: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Broad near wall and upper rock planes remain readable; limited reverse ridge is still visible. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 93 / window 0027: A wall; B present; C present. Reverse broad rock wall fills the turn while forward exposes a valley and coastal panorama. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence. Raised-side extent on the bend is unresolved.

Station 94 / window 0027: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Close face switches sides across the paired view, with broad upper rock planes and an open outlook. A separate distant terrain/panorama region is not clear enough to confirm C.

Station 95 / window 0028: A wall; B present; C absent. Local wall and reverse bank/contact remain readable below large exposed faces and skyline context. No distinct farther terrain region is established beyond the dominant face itself.

Station 96 / window 0028: A wall; B present; C absent. Near right cut and reverse contact bank sit under a substantial rocky face and distant outline. No distinct farther terrain region is established beyond the dominant face itself.

Station 97 / window 0029: A bank; B present; C absent. Low contact banks frame a broad, nearly vertical upper face; both views are enclosed by slopes. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 98 / window 0029: A bank; B present; C absent. Same low-bank and dominant upper-wall combination persists without a clear distant panorama. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 99 / window 0030: A wall; B present; C absent. High broad face dominates above local banks; the opposite view remains within the rock enclosure. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 100 / window 0030: A wall; B present; C absent. Original forward PNG confirms a dominant tall right wall and substantial descending left bank/contact. Raised-side code is right only; descending left contact still warrants near-detail attention. Projecting wall contours and the sea opening do not establish a separate distant C terrain region.

Station 101 / window 0030: A wall; B present; C absent. Tall right wall and upper planes are prominent; forward begins to reveal the coast and outer ridge. The visible horizon is not a separate distant terrain region; roadside wall contours are not C. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 102 / window 0031: A wall; B present; C absent. Close walls flank the forward road, with a jagged side outline and open coast beyond. The visible horizon is not a separate distant terrain region; roadside wall contours are not C.

Station 103 / window 0031: A wall; B present; C absent. The narrow wall-lined stretch retains readable wall contours and a coastal panorama. The visible horizon is not a separate distant terrain region; roadside wall contours are not C.

Station 104 / window 0032: A bank; B absent; C present. Low sloped banks frame the bend; broad hillside and ridge matter more than a single dominant wall. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 105 / window 0032: A bank; B absent; C present. Banks and ground contact remain close; reverse shows broad slope composition and skyline. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 106 / window 0033: A wall; B present; C present. Tall right wall and reverse-left face are dominant, while the forward opens to a coastal ridge. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.

Station 107 / window 0033: A wall; B present; C present. Close tall wall continues; paired view shows the wall-lined corridor and an open coastal outlook. Side codes include raised banks/walls only; descending contact remains separate near-detail evidence.
Station 108 / window 0034: A wall; B present; C present. Tall roadside faces swap sides; reverse also shows a broad recessed cliff while forward opens to a distant peak and horizon.
Station 109 / window 0034: A wall; B present; C present. High near faces remain readable in both directions; reverse cliff divisions and forward isolated skyline remain visible.
Station 110 / window 0035: A wall; B absent; C present. Forward bend has lower banks on both sides; reverse left face is close, with an open distant ridge and horizon.
Station 111 / window 0035: A bank; B absent; C present. The banks lower around the bend; reverse left slope still exposes local plane changes and the distant outlook stays open.
Station 112 / window 0035: A bank; B uncertain; C present. Low banks frame the curve; a partly visible larger rock mass needs original-frame review to separate broad-face demand from skyline.

Station 113 / window 0035: A bank; B present; C uncertain. Original forward PNG shows a raised bank on the right and descending inner ground on the left; the large upper peak has readable face divisions. Reverse bank sides remain contact-sheet observations. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity remains uncertain; the same broad face outline or sea horizon alone does not establish C.

Station 114 / window 0035: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Near right face rises at the bend; the forward peak and reverse massif retain visible shelves and broad faces. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.
Station 115 / window 0035: A wall; B present; C present. High right roadside face and two reverse banks frame a broad layered basin and an isolated peak.

Station 116 / window 0036: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Road follows a steep right face; reverse shows a large articulated cliff beyond the left near wall, with distant horizon in forward. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 117 / window 0036: A wall; B present; C uncertain. Steep near face remains prominent; reverse cliff recesses and shelves remain legible beyond it. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 118 / window 0037: A bank; B present; C uncertain. Forward bank is lower, while the reverse opens toward a large cliff face and sea-facing landscape. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 119 / window 0037: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Near sloping banks are clear; the reverse background face is partly hidden so its dominant-wall requirement is uncertain. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 120 / window 0038: A wall; B uncertain; C absent. Tight paired bend views expose near side walls; upper terrain is cropped and does not establish a panorama. No distinct distant landform panorama is established in this pair; sea alone is not counted.

Station 121 / window 0038: A wall; B uncertain; C absent. Near wall and bend contact remain clear in both directions; cropped upper faces need a wider or original view. No distinct distant landform panorama is established in this pair; sea alone is not counted.

Station 122 / window 0039: A bank; B uncertain; C absent. The curve is enclosed by sloping roadside forms; no clearly open skyline is visible in this pair. No distinct distant landform panorama is established in this pair; sea alone is not counted.

Station 123 / window 0039: A bank; B present; C uncertain. A near left bank contrasts with a broad forward right-hand rock face; reverse reveals intermediate slope structure. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 124 / window 0039: A bank; B present; C uncertain. The forward opposite face retains large divisions above another road level; near bank switches sides in reverse. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 125 / window 0039: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Clear near-bank planes and multiple road levels; larger upper faces are cropped or small enough to leave B uncertain. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 126 / window 0039: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Near slope contact remains readable and the forward horizon is open; dominant broad-face readability is unresolved at contact-sheet scale. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.
Station 127 / window 0039: A wall; B uncertain; C present. Left roadside face becomes steeper; reverse frames show terraces and upper terrain but insufficient broad-face detail for definite B.
Station 128 / window 0040: A wall; B uncertain; C present. Tall close left face continues into the next window; reverse landscape remains partly cropped.
Station 129 / window 0040: A wall; B present; C present. The near left wall occupies a large image area with distinct planes; forward opening also retains distant skyline context.

Station 130 / window 0041: A wall; B uncertain; C absent. Close right and reverse left faces flank a high road; dark road regions do not establish their cause or surface identity. No distinct distant landform panorama is established in this pair; sea alone is not counted.

Station 131 / window 0041: A bank; B uncertain; C absent. Sloping near banks remain clear despite dark road regions; reverse opens toward the horizon and partial wider terrain. No distinct distant landform panorama is established in this pair; sea alone is not counted.

Station 132 / window 0041: A bank; B uncertain; C absent. Paired near banks flank a raised-looking road view; the reverse opens to horizon but upper broad-face evidence is incomplete. No distinct distant landform panorama is established in this pair; sea alone is not counted.

Station 133 / window 0042: A bank; B uncertain; C absent. Long right bank and reverse left bank have readable local planes; basin terrain fills the forward background without a clear isolated wall. No distinct distant landform panorama is established in this pair; sea alone is not counted.

Station 134 / window 0042: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Continuous sloping roadside forms remain prominent; reverse horizon and wider hillside provide landscape context. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 135 / window 0042: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Near bank height reduces along the straight; larger background terrain remains visible but wall dominance is unclear. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 136 / window 0042: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Readable bank contact continues; broad rough terrain beyond it warrants review without automatically counting every outcrop as B. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 137 / window 0042: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Near sloping bank remains visible in both directions; upper landforms and a reverse horizon stay partly exposed. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 138 / window 0042: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Forward bank reaches the approaching bend; reverse upper terrain is substantial but its readable broad faces need original pixels. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.
Station 139 / window 0043: A bank; B absent; C present. Banks frame a tight bend; wider reverse outline is visible, but no distinct dominant broad wall is established.
Station 140 / window 0043: A bank; B absent; C present. Close sloping forms and the reverse left bank carry contact detail; surrounding low ridges supply context rather than a dominant face.

Station 141 / window 0043: A wall; B uncertain; C uncertain. The reverse left bank presents a steep plane while the forward turn opens toward a larger rough slope; B remains uncertain. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 142 / window 0044: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Forward low banks open toward sea and hillside; reverse left near bank is clearer than the cropped background forms. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 143 / window 0044: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Both views show near low banks and broad terrain; distant or cropped features do not yet establish a dominant wall. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 144 / window 0044: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Low banks border both directions; forward hillside and sea opening contrast with cropped reverse terrain. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 145 / window 0044: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. A clear near right bank swaps to the left in reverse; broad basin terrain remains partly clipped. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 146 / window 0045: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Near right slope and reverse left bank are readable; an open horizon and distant basin provide panoramic context. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 147 / window 0045: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. The same station pair shows near sloping forms and a long open outlook; larger reverse faces need closer inspection. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.

Station 148 / window 0045: A bank; B uncertain; C uncertain. Low right bank and reverse left bank remain near; broad terrain is visible without enough contact-sheet detail to confirm B. Separate distant-ridge/panorama identity is uncertain; an open horizon or the same broad face outline alone does not establish C.
Station 149 / window 0046: A wall; B present; C present. Steep near bank is separate from a prominent forward cliff with readable large divisions; reverse shows a small distant ridge.
